definition: In computer science, computational learning theory (or just learning theory) is a subfield of artificial intelligence devoted to studying the design and analysis of machine learning algorithms.
details: In computer science, computational learning theory (or just learning theory) is a subfield of artificial intelligence devoted to studying the design and analysis of machine learning algorithms.

explainer.lead: Computational learning theory is the part of artificial intelligence that studies how machine-learning algorithms are designed and analysed. It matters because building a learning system involves more than getting one program to work: the algorithm itself can be examined as an object of study.

tiers.eli5: Imagine trying different ways to learn a game from examples. Computational learning theory studies the learning methods themselves—how they are built and how we can examine them—rather than focusing on just one game. It is like studying recipes for learning, not only tasting one finished dish.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer can use this perspective when designing a machine-learning algorithm and analysing its learning behaviour, rather than judging only a single implementation or run. A common pitfall is treating the field as a software package or a fixed training procedure; it is a research area concerned with algorithms.
tiers.paperLevel: Computational learning theory is formally described as the subfield of artificial intelligence devoted to the design and analysis of machine-learning algorithms. Its subject is therefore algorithms and their analysis, rather than one particular model, dataset, or application.

explainer.example: Suppose two algorithms are proposed for learning to sort emails from labelled examples. Computational learning theory concerns how each algorithm is designed and what its analysis can establish, rather than being the email dataset or either trained filter itself.

usedIn.name: Machine-learning algorithm design
usedIn.detail: Provides a field dedicated to studying how algorithms that learn are constructed.

usedIn.name: Artificial intelligence research
usedIn.detail: Forms a subfield concerned with analysing machine-learning algorithms.

explainer.intuition: Instead of asking only whether a learning program succeeds at one task, computational learning theory turns attention to the learning algorithm itself. It studies both how such algorithms are designed and how they can be analysed.
howItWorks: Choose a machine-learning algorithm as the object of study.
Examine how the algorithm is designed to learn.
Analyse the algorithm rather than treating it as an unquestioned black box.
Use that study to understand learning algorithms as a subject within artificial intelligence.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives artificial intelligence a dedicated way to study machine-learning algorithms instead of evaluating only individual applications. That focus connects algorithm design with analysis.
misconceptions: It is not a single machine-learning algorithm; it is a field that studies algorithms.
It is not just the practice of training a model, because its concerns include algorithm design and analysis.
It is not separate from artificial intelligence; it is a subfield of it.
